security_spec.violation_condition: OpenSBI's delegate_traps() writes the entire mideleg CSR using a hardcoded bitmask (MIP_SSIP|MIP_STIP|MIP_SEIP|sbi_pmu_irq_mask()) that has no defined bit for interrupt 14 (LAMBI). On hardware implementing Ssamb, this explicit csr_write(CSR_MIDELEG, ...) clobbers any prior delegation of bit 14 with 0 (M-mode). If mie[14] is set—by bootloader residual, HSM non-retentive suspend restore race, or errant S-mode via mvien alias—a LAMBI traps to M-mode where sbi_trap_handler() dispatches on mcause and has no case for cause 14, hitting the default error path (panic or hang). The clear-MIE-before-mret sequence in the PMU overflow codepath (sbi_pmu.c:344) specifically clears only the PMU irq_mask, not bit 14, so if mie[14] is set and mip[14] is asserted, returning to S-mode without clearing mie[14] creates a re-entrant trap loop.
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: full-register csr_write(CSR_MIDELEG, <hex_or_bitwise_OR_mask>) that lacks a defined constant for major interrupt ID 14; any csr_clear(CSR_MIE, <partial_mask>) that does not include bit 14 yet leaves mie[14] set during mret; grep for 'CSR_MIDELEG' full-writes and 'CSR_MIE' partial-clear operations
security_spec.summary: Ssamb defines interrupt 14 as local LAMBI; OpenSBI clobbers mideleg[14]=0 with hardcoded mask lacking IRQ_14 constant, has no M-mode cause-14 dispatch, and partial-mie-clear operations don't mask bit 14—risking unhandled trap loop if mie[14] is set by residual state on Ssamb hardware
